newsitem.title: USA: Conn. prosecutors mull action on Kelly's bond.
newsitem.headline: Conn. prosecutors mull action on Kelly's bond.

text.p: Connecticut prosecutors said on Friday they will likely ask a judge to revoke the $1 million bond of convicted rapist Alex Kelly because they fear the former fugitive will flee again.
"I wouldn't doubt it -- that's what we feel should happen," a state's attorney's official told Reuters.

Kelly, 30, was convicted on Thursday of raping a 16-year-old girl in a car 11 years ago. He was later released on a bond of $1 million, secured by properties owned by his parents in Darien, Connecticut.

Stamford Superior Court Judge Kevin Tierney set sentencing for July 24. Kelly, who had claimed the sex was consensual, is due back in court on June 26, when Tierney will review conditions of the bond.

The former high school wrestling star turned international fugitive faces up to 20 years in jail. Tierney ordered him released on bond over the vehement objections of prosecutors, who cited Kelly's eight-year flight from justice.

Kelly fled the United States just before his original scheduled trial in 1987, embarking on an odyssey through 15 countries including time spent on the ski slopes of Europe. He said he fled because he feared he would not get a fair trial.
Authorities have said his travels were financed by his wealthy parents.

"There is no legitimate reason for that bond not to be revoked," prosecutor Bruce Hudock told reporters on Thursday. "(Kelly) has proven that he can just go before. I see nothing that will hold him back at this point."

Under terms of the bond, Kelly remains under virtual house arrest. He can leave his parents' home for doctor's visits or meetings with lawyers or to attend college classes, and then only in the company of at least one parent.
He must also continue to wear the same electronic bracelet that has monitored his curfews since his return to the United States in 1995, after his surrender in Switzerland.
